user.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
I built the book tracker. It's a small Node server that uses nothing but Node's built-in modules, so there's nothing to install to run it. Pages are plain HTML and every book is saved to a JSON file. The tests pass, and a manual run with a restart kept the books.

Run it with `npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000.

- **Home page:** shows "Currently reading" (newest first, each with a "Mark finished" button) and "Finished" (with the date you finished). The "Add a book" form is below them. Title and author are required and notes are optional. If you leave a required field empty, you get an error message and what you typed stays in the form.
- **Book page (`/books/<id>`):** shows the title, author, your notes, and whether you're still reading it or when you finished. You can mark it finished from there too. There's a "Share" box with the full link to copy. Each book gets a random 8-character ID, so links are hard to guess but not private: anyone with the link can see that book.
- **Saving:** books go to `data/books.json`. Every save writes a temporary file first and then swaps it in, so a crash mid-save won't break the file. If the file ever gets damaged, the app won't start and tells you why, rather than overwriting your data. You can change the port and file location with the `PORT` and `DATA_FILE` environment variables.

The code is in `server.js`, `src/store.js` (saving), `src/app.js` (pages and form handling) and `src/views.js` (HTML). I also added `start` and `test` scripts to `package.json`, and added `data/` to `.gitignore` so your reading list doesn't get committed to git. If you want it in git, delete that line.

**Checks:**
- `npx vitest run`: 7 of 7 tests passed, exit code 0. They cover adding, finishing, the book page and share link, keeping books after a restart, required fields, safe display of anything typed into the form, missing pages, and refusing to overwrite a damaged file.
- Manual check: I started the real server, added a book with `curl`, stopped it and started it again. The book page still loaded with the right title, author and share link, and the home page returned 200. I then deleted the test `data/` folder, and no server is left running.

There are no accounts or passwords, so anyone who can reach the server can add books or mark them finished. That's fine on your own computer, but don't put it on the public internet as is. Notes are also written only when you add a book; there's no way to edit them later. That would be a small next step if you want it.

cat /tmp/s2.log
EOF
bash /tmp/smoke.sh; ls data; rm -rf data; git status --short"}
